newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's ruling party set to lose capital - poll.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's ruling party set to lose capital - poll.

text.p: Mexico's conservative opposition National Action Party (PAN) is by far the favourite among voters to win the mayorship of Mexico City next year, a new poll released on Friday showed.

The long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) is in last place among the main parties, behind the leftist Democratic Revolution Party (PRD), according to the Indemerc-Louis Harris poll of 800 residents of the capital.

The poll, which had a 3.5 percent margin of error, showed the PAN with 40 percent support, up from 37 percent last month, while the PRD had 23 percent, up from 22 percent in October. The PRI was flat at 12 percent.
Other parties were also flat at 5 percent while undecided voters fell to 20 percent from 23 percent.

Residents of Mexico City, one of the biggest urban sprawls in the world, will be able vote for the first time next July to choose their mayor, who was previously a presidential appointment and always from the PRI.
None of the parties has named its candidate yet for the post, the formal name of which will change from regent to governor.
